title: Hover preview is cut off at 190px, and the hidden lines cannot be reached with a mouse
repro: 1280x800. New Space / Initial Feasibility, Wildfire, LEO. Add 12U CubeSat frame, Spin stabilisation, Optical camera, Small solar panel, UHF radio, Basic computer. Open [data-key=bin-instrument] and hover [data-key=part-sar-radar]. Then move the mouse onto the #preview box to scroll it.
expected: All of the preview is readable, and the red 'Causes:' lines most of all, because the preview exists to show them.
actual: #preview has clientHeight 182 and scrollHeight 418, so more than half of it is clipped. Only the first 'Causes:' line shows, and it is cut through the middle. Three more lines stay hidden: payload overload, the second instrument slot and power. Moving the mouse into the box to scroll fires pointerleave on the card, and the preview resets to 'Point at a part to see what it would change.' A mouse user can never read the clipped lines.
evidence: Script t4.js logged {client:182, scroll:418} and four Causes lines in the DOM. After the mouse moved into the preview it read 'IF YOU CLICK | | Point at a part to see what it would change.' Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/build/t4-preview-overflow.png. Web fonts were blocked in this run, but the gap is large enough that real fonts would not close it.
cause: css/style.css:315 sets `.preview { height: 190px; overflow-y: auto; }`. js/ui-design.js:1988 clears state.hover on any mouse pointerleave from the card.
fix_hint: Let the preview grow (use max-height with the sticky column, or put the fixes and causes first). Alternatively keep the last previewed part while the pointer is over #preview.

verdict.note: Ran v01.js at 1280x800 and 1920x1080: New Space / Initial Feasibility, Wildfire, LEO, with cubesat-12u, spin-stabilised, optical-camera, solar-small, radio-uhf and obc-basic, then hovered part-sar-radar. #preview measured clientHeight 182 against scrollHeight 418 at both sizes. The first Causes line sits at 171-217px inside the 182px box, so it is cut through the middle; the three Causes lines below it (body slots, power, smear) are hidden. Moving the mouse into the box in 20 steps reset it to 'IF YOU CLICK | Point at a part to see what it would change.', so a mouse user cannot scroll it. A wheel over the box left scrollTop at 0. Keyboard users cannot scroll it either: #preview has tabIndex -1, and Tab moves to the next card, which replaces the preview. Font check: fonts were blocked (Courier New fallback, wider than VT323), so v01c.js forced white-space:nowrap on every line as a lower bound that ignores wrapping. It still measured scroll 280 against client 182, with only 1 of 4 Causes lines fitting, so real fonts will not fix this. Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/verify-build/v01-1280-hover.png. Root cause: css/style.css:315 (.preview { height: 190px; overflow-y: auto }) and js/ui-design.js:1988 (any mouse pointerleave from the card sets state.hover = null and redraws the preview). A player can work around it by clicking the part and reading PROBLEMS, which is why this is major, not blocker.

title: On a phone the first tap shows its preview about 1000px off-screen, so the tap seems to do nothing (same at 200% zoom with a mouse)
repro: Playwright 'iPhone 13' profile (390x664). New Space / Initial Feasibility, Wildfire, LEO. Tap [data-key=bin-instrument], scroll to [data-key=part-thermal-imager] and tap it once. Second repro: viewport 640x400 at DPR 2 (200% zoom of 1280x800), hover the same card with the mouse.
expected: The first tap (the preview tap) gives visible feedback near the card, saying what adding it would change, as SPEC 3 Build requires.
actual: The preview renders at top=-835 to -1234px in a 664px viewport, far above the shelf. A pixel diff of the viewport before and after the first tap shows only the card border lightening, the same as its hover style. aria-pressed stays false. At 640x400 the hovered card's preview sits at top=-897 / -726. After the second tap the bench with the add animation is also off-screen (benchTop -1175), and the bars sit about 2000px further down.
evidence: Scripts t14.js and t3.js logged {previewTop:-835, previewBottom:-645, vh:664, pressed:'false', preview:'ADD THERMAL INFRARED IMAGER'}. t19.js logged '640x400 hover optical-camera {top:-897,...}'. Before/after image: (scratch)/sweep/build/t14-phone-first-tap-side-by-side.png. 200% zoom shot: (scratch)/sweep/build/t19-zoom640-hover.png
cause: css/style.css:316 makes .preview sticky only at min-width 930px. js/ui-design.js:2117 puts the preview above the shelf in a single column, so below 930px it scrolls away. The tapped card gets no 'armed' state either.
fix_hint: Below 930px, make the preview sticky to the bottom of the viewport, or show it inline under the tapped card, and mark the armed card.

verdict.note: Ran v02.js with the Playwright 'iPhone 13' profile: New Space, Wildfire, LEO. Tapped bin-instrument, scrolled to part-thermal-imager and tapped once. Result: {previewTop:-835, previewBottom:-645, cardTop:243, vh:664, pressed:'false', preview h3:'ADD THERMAL INFRARED IMAGER', card class 'part'}. The preview text is rendered, but about 1,000px above the viewport. A pixel diff of before and after the first tap shows only the card border lightening, the same as the hover/focus style; there is no armed state. Side-by-side image: (scratch)/sweep/verify-build/v02-phone-side-by-side.png. The second tap adds the part (pressed true), but the bench sits at top -1175 and the bars at 2062, so the result of the click is off-screen too. At 640x400 with DPR 2 (200% zoom), hovering part-optical-camera put the preview at top -897 / bottom -707 in a 400px viewport (v02-zoom640-hover.png in the same folder). Root cause: css/style.css:316 makes the preview sticky only at min-width 930px. js/ui-design.js:2117 puts drawPreview() above payoutLine and the shelf in .bench-col, which is a single column below 930px (css:690), so it scrolls away. Nothing is blocked, because the second tap still works, but the preview step SPEC 3 Build asks for is never seen on phones.

title: In the 1964 Nimbus era with a sun-synchronous orbit, every hover preview says 'Causes: ... needs 80 m/s of thrust', but no real check says so
repro: Open the Nimbus / Initial Feasibility mission [data-key=start-nimbus-training]. Pick Weather, then Sun-synchronous. Add drum-body, spin-stabilised, vidicon-camera, silicon-cells, vhf-telemetry, tape-recorder. Hover any part, for example [data-key=part-command-timer] or [data-key=part-nicad-battery], or hover spin stabilisation to preview removing it.
expected: No delta-v cause. runChecks waives the 80 m/s disposal burn before 1995 (DISPOSAL_RULE_YEAR), and the real PROBLEMS list shows no NOT ENOUGH THRUST.
actual: Every preview ends with 'Causes: Sun-synchronous polar orbit needs 80 m/s of thrust from the spacecraft, but it has only 0 m/s. Add propulsion or cut mass.' In 1964 all three propulsion parts say 'Arrives in 1998', so the advice is impossible. The real PROBLEMS list at the same moment shows only PICTURES SMEAR and NO SHADOW POWER.
evidence: t20.js in-page check returned {year:1964, dvNeededDesign:0, dvNeededNoYear:80, withYearBlockers:['no-launcher'], noYearBlockers:['no-launcher','delta-v'], previewCauses:['delta-v']}. t21.js preview text: 'ADD CLOCK AND COMMAND RECEIVER | +0.5 kg, +$0.02M | Causes: Sun-synchronous polar orbit needs 80 m/s...'. For the screenshot only, the preview height was set to auto so the whole text shows: (scratch)/sweep/build/t21-nimbus-preview-full.png. Campaign designs are not affected, because `campaign` is copied.
cause: js/game.js:723-724. previewToggle builds `after` from tier, objective, orbit, launcher, parts and campaign, but drops `year` and `era`. designYear(after) returns null, and dvNeeded falls back to 80 m/s.
fix_hint: Copy `year` and `era` into `after` (better: shallow-copy the whole design and replace parts).

verdict.note: Ran v03.js: start-nimbus-training (status '1964'), Weather, Sun-synchronous, with drum-body, spin-stabilised, vidicon-camera, silicon-cells, vhf-telemetry and tape-recorder. The PROBLEMS panel reads only 'PICTURES SMEAR, NO SHADOW POWER'. Hovering command-timer, nicad-battery or spin-stabilised (remove) gives 'Causes: Sun-synchronous polar orbit needs 80 m/s of thrust from the spacecraft, but it has only 0 m/s. Add propulsion or cut mass.' on each. All three propulsion cards are disabled with 'Arrives in 1998', so the advice cannot be followed. An in-page API check on the same design returned {year:1964, runChecks(after with year) blockers:['no-launcher'], previewToggle causes:['delta-v']}. Root cause: js/game.js:723-724. previewToggle builds `after` from tier, objective, orbit, launcher, parts and campaign but drops `year` and `era`, so designYear(after) is null and dvNeeded (game.js:183-186) skips the pre-1995 waiver. Missing year/era also means `after` skips the era part-locked checks. Graded major rather than minor because this is false, impossible advice on every hover in the era's flagship mission, and nothing on screen corrects it (contrast build-04).

title: A legal battery-only design shows a full red POWER bar '0 / 0 W, Nothing makes power yet'; in the 1957 campaign it can never go out of the red
screen: 3 Build, 4 Launch vehicle, 5 Readiness (IGY standalone and the 1957 campaign)
repro: Title: [data-key=campaign-training], then START A MISSION. Pick Radiation, then LEO. Add explorer-body, spin-stabilised, cosmic-ray-counter, mercury-battery, minitrack-beacon, command-timer. (Same in standalone [data-key=start-igy-training].)
expected: runChecks only warns (BATTERY ONLY), and Readiness reads 'GO, WITH 1 WARNING'. SPEC says a bar is red only when over the limit, so the bar should not show this design as failing. The battery does make power, so 'Nothing makes power yet' is also wrong.
actual: The POWER bar has class 'bar bad' at width 100%, text '0 / 0 W', note 'Nothing makes power yet'. The Build hint on the same screen says 'Add parts until every required column has one and the four bars stay out of the red.' In the 1957 campaign every solar part is disabled ('Needs research: Silicon solar cells'), so the player cannot follow the hint. (Draw is 0.1 W, rounded to 0.)
evidence: t20.js: 'power bar class bar bad width: 100%', 'problems: BATTERY ONLY | Why | WARN', and the power bin lists part-silicon-cells, part-solar-small and others as [disabled: ... Needs research ...]. t13.js on the same design at Readiness: 'verdict GO, WITH 1 WARNING'. Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/build/t20-campaign-1957-power-bar.png and t16-igy-bars.png in the same folder.
cause: js/ui-design.js:1637-1638. When power_gen_w is 0, any draw gives fill 1 and class ' bad'. The note keys only on power_gen_w and ignores battery_wh or batteryLifeMonths.
fix_hint: When the design is battery-only (batteryLifeMonths(d) !== null), show a battery state such as amber with 'Battery only: about N days'. Do not show red.

verdict.note: Ran v04.js. In a new campaign (campaign-training, 1957), START A MISSION, Radiation, LEO, with explorer-body, spin-stabilised, cosmic-ray-counter, mercury-battery, minitrack-beacon and command-timer: the POWER bar has class 'bar bad', width 100% and text 'POWER | 0 / 0 W | Nothing makes power yet' on Build, Launch vehicle and Readiness. PROBLEMS shows only 'BATTERY ONLY ... WARN', and Readiness says 'GO, WITH 1 WARNING' with LAUNCH enabled. The same bar appears in standalone IGY. getTotals: power_draw_w 0.1, power_gen_w 0, battery_wh 160, margins.power null. In the 1957 campaign every solar part is disabled ('Needs research: Silicon solar cells' and similar), so the Build hint (data/hints.js:46, 'keep the four bars out of the red') cannot be followed on the first campaign mission. Research unlocks solar later; standalone IGY does offer silicon-cells. Framing: SPEC:883 makes the bar draw against generation, so 0.1 against 0 is literally 'over'. The bug is the clash with SPEC:422 (battery-only may launch and is a warning, not a blocker). On top of that, '0 / 0 W' hides the 0.1 W draw, and 'Nothing makes power yet' is shown next to a 160 Wh battery. Root cause: js/ui-design.js:1636-1638. When margins.power is null and draw > 0, fill is 1 and the class is ' bad'; the note checks only power_gen_w and ignores battery_wh. Minor, because the team line ('No solar panel. The battery runs out...') and the GO verdict make the situation clear. Screenshots: (scratch)/sweep/verify-build/v04-campaign-build.png and v04-campaign-review.png in the same folder.

title: OVER BUDGET 'FIX >' sends you to the Rocket Yard when no rocket is picked and the parts alone are over budget
repro: Open New Space / Point Design ($18M; you need best_stars.standard >= 2 to unlock it). Pick Wildfire, then LEO. Add parts until the parts cost more than $18M (22.65 here). Do not pick a rocket. Visit the Rocket Yard, then go to the Launch Pad through the map. Click FIX on 'OVER BUDGET'.
expected: FIX goes to the Workshop, where the money was spent. The game's own route logic (fixPlace) sends you there, and so do the objective line and the GO TO button.
actual: FIX opens 4 · LAUNCH VEHICLE. On that screen the objective line says 'OBJECTIVE: Go to the Workshop and build the satellite.' and the button reads 'GO TO WORKSHOP >'. Every rocket keeps the design over budget (rideshare 23/18, small 30.15/18, heavy 92.4/18, thor-able 28.65/18).
evidence: t15.js output: 'OVER BUDGET FIX -> 4 · LAUNCH VEHICLE | objective line: OBJECTIVE: Go to the Workshop and build the satellite. | GO TO: GO TO WORKSHOP >'. Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/build/t15-budget-fix-launcher.png
cause: js/ui-design.js:1680 checkList uses `FIX_SCREEN[row.c.id] || "build"`. The fixPlace(check, d) helper at js/ui-design.js:2235 sends mass and budget to Build when there is no launcher, but checkList does not use it.
fix_hint: In checkList, use `var target = fixPlace(row.c, design);`.

verdict.note: Ran v05.js: New Space / Point Design ($18M; progress set with best_stars.standard 3), Wildfire, LEO. Added parts to $21.6M with no rocket, walked to the Rocket Yard with GO TO ROCKET YARD, then took the map to the Launch Pad. The checks include OVER BUDGET with aria-label 'Fix on the launcher screen: Cost is $21.55M but the budget is $18M.' Clicking FIX opened '4 · LAUNCH VEHICLE'. On that screen the objective reads 'OBJECTIVE: Go to the Workshop and build the satellite.' and the nav button reads 'GO TO WORKSHOP >', so the game sends you somewhere and then tells you to leave. Root cause: js/ui-design.js:1680 uses `FIX_SCREEN[row.c.id] || "build"` and FIX_SCREEN (ui-design.js:50-55) maps budget to launcher. fixPlace() at ui-design.js:2235-2237 already sends mass and budget to build when there is no launcher, and the waypoint uses it, but checkList does not. Note: the SPEC readiness table (SPEC:925) maps `budget` to 4 Launch vehicle, adding '(mass and budget can also be fixed on Build)'. So FIX going to the Rocket Yard follows the SPEC table, and the real bug is the clash with the game's own route logic (SPEC:800). Changing FIX to use fixPlace needs a SPEC decision, not only a code change. Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/verify-build/v05-fix-budget.png

title: MASS bar says 'Pick a rocket to see the limit' while a rocket is already picked (one that cannot reach the orbit)
repro: Pick Weather, then LEO, and build a complete satellite. On the Rocket Yard pick [data-key=rocket-thor-able]. Through the map, go back to the Tracking Station and choose Sun-synchronous. Open the Rocket Yard or the Launch Pad.
expected: The mass bar or its note says the chosen rocket (Thor-Able) cannot reach this orbit, matching the ROCKET CANNOT REACH line.
actual: Mass bar: 'MASS 38.5 KG' with the note 'Pick a rocket to see the limit'. At the same time the Thor-Able card shows CANNOT REACH and aria-pressed=true, and Readiness lists 'Rocket: Thor-Able'.
evidence: t11.js: 'bars on launcher: MASS | 38.5 KG | Pick a rocket to see the limit | ...', 'thor-able card: THOR-ABLE | CANNOT REACH ... pressed true', 'review facts: ... Rocket | Thor-Able'. Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/build/t11-cannot-reach.png
cause: js/ui-design.js:1635 picks the note from `t.capacity_kg` alone. getTotals returns capacity 0 both when no rocket is chosen and when the rocket cannot reach.
fix_hint: When design.launcher is set and capacity is 0, show e.g. '<rocket> cannot reach this orbit'.

verdict.note: Ran v06.js: Weather, LEO, a complete smallsat build, Thor-Able picked (mass bar 'MASS | 39.6 / 130 KG'). Then took the map to the Tracking Station, chose Sun-synchronous and returned to the Rocket Yard. Mass bar: 'MASS | 39.6 KG | Pick a rocket to see the limit'. The Thor-Able card reads 'CANNOT REACH', with aria-pressed true and disabled. Readiness shows the same bar note while its checks list 'ROCKET CANNOT REACH'. Root cause: js/ui-design.js:1635 picks the note from t.capacity_kg alone, and getTotals (game.js:347) returns capacity 0 both with no rocket and with a rocket that cannot reach. This is a gap in the SPEC rather than a code slip: SPEC:883 says 'pick a rocket' while capacity_kg is 0, and the code does exactly that. The ROCKET CANNOT REACH line and the card tag on the same screens tell the player what is wrong, so this is polish, not minor. Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/verify-build/v06-cannot-reach.png

title: Small non-zero values are shown as 0 (part cards, preview deltas, DATA HOME bar next to a DATA LOST warning)
screen: 3 Build (all eras, worst in 1958 to 1964), bars on 3 to 5
repro: (a) IGY: open the instrument and comms bins and read the Geiger counter and Minitrack cards. (b) New Space: hover [data-key=part-obc-basic]. (c) IGY Radiation LEO with explorer-body, spin-stabilised, cosmic-ray-counter, scintillation-counter, mercury-battery, minitrack-beacon, command-timer: read the DATA HOME bar.
expected: SPEC: 'Show only fields that are not 0'. A field that is shown has a non-zero value, so it should not read 0, and the bar should agree with the DATA LOST warning.
actual: (a) 'Geiger counter package ... 2.3 kg · 0 W draw · 0 GB/d made', '108 MHz Minitrack beacon ... 0 W draw · 0 GB/d sent'. (b) '+0.1 kg, +0 W draw, +$0.01M' for a +0.4 W change. (c) DATA HOME reads '0 / 0 GB/DAY' with an amber bar at 41.7%, while the warning says 'Instruments make 0.00006 GB a day but only 0.000025 GB reaches the ground.'
evidence: t8.js: instrument and comms card text. t1.js: obc-basic preview, where previewToggle delta.power_draw_w is 0.4. t16.js: 'IGY data bar: ... DATA HOME | 0 / 0 GB/DAY', class 'bar warn', 'width: 41.66%'. Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/build/t16-igy-bars.png
cause: js/ui-design.js:1946-1948 (partStats uses num(v,0) for watts and num(v) at 1 decimal for GB), :2010 (preview watts at 0 places), and resourceBars DATA HOME uses num() at 1 place. num() rounds with maximumFractionDigits and has no significant-figure fallback.
fix_hint: Format small values with significant figures (e.g. '<0.1 W', '20 kB/d') or switch units for tiny data rates.

verdict.note: Ran v07.js. (a) IGY cards: Geiger counter reads '2.3 kg · 0 W draw · 0 GB/d made' (data power_draw_w 0.05, data_gb_day 0.00002), and the Minitrack beacon reads '0.3 kg · 0 W draw · 0 GB/d sent' (0.06 W, 0.001 GB/d). This breaks SPEC:879, 'Show only fields that are not 0'. (b) New Space: the obc-basic card reads '0 W draw', and its hover preview reads '+0.1 kg, +0 W draw, +$0.01M' while the same preview's Causes line says 'Parts draw 0.4 W' (delta.power_draw_w 0.4). (c) IGY with explorer-body, spin-stabilised, cosmic-ray-counter, scintillation-counter, mercury-battery, minitrack-beacon and command-timer: the DATA HOME bar reads '0 / 0 GB/DAY', class 'bar warn', width 41.67%, while the DATA LOST check says 'Instruments make 0.00006 GB a day but only 0.000025 GB reaches the ground.' Root cause: js/ui-design.js:1946-1947 (num(v,0) for W, num(v) for GB), :2010 (preview W at 0 places) and :1641 (DATA HOME with num()). num() at ui-design.js:767 rounds by decimal places and has no significant-figure fallback. Screenshot: (scratch)/sweep/verify-build/v07-igy-bars.png

title: Hover preview misses a new body-slot overflow (or its fix) when another slot is already over
repro: New Space, Wildfire, LEO. Add the 12U CubeSat frame (1 instrument and 1 radio slot), Optical camera, Thermal imager and UHF radio. Open the RADIO bin and hover [data-key=part-radio-sband].
expected: 'Causes: The 12U CubeSat frame has room for 1 comms part (you fitted 2).' Adding the radio creates this blocker.
actual: The preview lists only '+0.3 kg, +10 W draw, +$0.03M, data home +1.6 GB/day', with no cause. runChecks on the design after adding shows both body-slots blockers (instrument and comms).
evidence: t16.js: previewToggle causes [] and afterSlots ['...room for 1 instrument part (you fitted 2).', '...room for 1 comms part (you fitted 2).'].
cause: js/game.js:745-746 compares checks by id only, and every slot overflow uses the same id 'body-slots' (js/game.js:546). The same applies to repeated 'part-locked' ids.
fix_hint: Compare id plus text, or give slot checks per-category ids such as body-slots-comms.

verdict.note: Ran v08.js: New Space, Wildfire, LEO, with cubesat-12u, optical-camera, thermal-imager and radio-uhf. PROBLEMS already shows 'BODY FULL: ...room for 1 instrument part (you fitted 2).' Hovering part-radio-sband shows only '+0.3 kg, +10 W draw, +$0.03M, data home +1.6 GB/day' with no Causes line. After clicking, PROBLEMS gains a second 'BODY FULL: ...room for 1 comms part (you fitted 2).' The reverse case fails the same way: hovering thermal-imager to remove it lists the payload and smear fixes but not the instrument BODY FULL fix, because the comms one still carries the same id. Root cause: js/game.js:745-746 compares checks by id only, and every slot overflow uses the id 'body-slots' (game.js:546). Repeated 'part-locked' ids would behave the same way.

title: The preview's aria-live region is replaced on every hover or focus, so screen readers are not told
repro: Hold a handle to #preview (aria-live='polite') and focus or hover [data-key=part-optical-camera]. Then attach a MutationObserver to the new #preview and hover another card.
expected: The live region stays in the DOM and its content changes, so assistive tech announces what the part would change. Keyboard users get the preview on focus, and this is how they would hear it.
actual: After each hover the old #preview node is detached (isConnected false) and a new one is inserted. The observer on the region recorded 0 mutations and was then disconnected. A newly inserted live region is usually not announced.
evidence: t20.js: 'old #preview still connected after hover? false | new node same? false', 'mutations inside the live region that existed before the hover: 0 | connected false'. Not checked with a real screen reader.
cause: js/ui-design.js:2027 `old.parentNode.replaceChild(drawPreview(), old)`. The whole Build screen is also rebuilt on every toggle.
fix_hint: Keep one #preview element and replace only its children.

verdict.note: Ran v09.js: kept a handle on #preview (aria-live='polite') with a MutationObserver on it, then focused part-optical-camera. Result: {oldConnected:false, same:false, muts:0}. The live region is replaced by a new node instead of having its content updated. Tab to the next card (part-topside-sounder) replaced it again. Newly inserted live regions are generally not announced, so keyboard and screen-reader users, who get the preview through onfocus, probably hear nothing. This is a DOM-level check only; I did not test with a real screen reader. Root cause: js/ui-design.js:2027, `old.parentNode.replaceChild(drawPreview(), old)`, which builds a fresh aria-live box at ui-design.js:2000 each time.

title: FIX for a missing part opens Build on the last-used bin, not the bin that is missing
repro: Build with only a thermal imager, pick the small launcher, go to the Launch Pad through the map, then click FIX on NO STRUCTURE, NO POWER or NO ATTITUDE.
expected: Build opens with the STRUCTURE, POWER or ATTITUDE bin selected.
actual: All three open with [data-key=bin-instrument] pressed and the heading 'AVAILABLE INSTRUMENTS'.
evidence: t22.js: 'NO STRUCTURE FIX -> open bin: bin-instrument', likewise for NO POWER and NO ATTITUDE.
cause: js/ui-design.js:1686 calls go(target) without setting state.bin from the check id (empty-<category>).
fix_hint: For empty-<cat> and body-slots, set state.bin before go('build').

verdict.note: Ran v10.js: New Space, Wildfire, LEO, with only thermal-imager added. Picked rocket-small and took the map to the Launch Pad. The checks include NO STRUCTURE, NO POWER, NO RADIO, NO COMPUTER and NO ATTITUDE. Clicking FIX on each opened Build with bin-instrument pressed and the heading 'AVAILABLE INSTRUMENTS', never the missing category. Root cause: the FIX onclick at js/ui-design.js:1686 calls go(target) without setting state.bin from the 'empty-<category>' id, and drawBuild falls back to the instrument bin. It costs the player one extra click, so this is real but polish.

title: Bin slot text reads '1 / 1 slots', and an over-full no-slot category shows '3 / 0 slots'
repro: IGY: add the Explorer body and one part of each kind. Then, in New Space with the Explorer body first, add three propulsion parts.
expected: Singular for one ('1 / 1 slot'). For a category the body has no room for, the existing wording 'N on board, no room'.
actual: 'INSTRUMENTS 1 / 1 slots', 'RADIO 1 / 1 slots'; 'PROPULSION 3 / 0 slots'. The code branch for 'on board, no room' never runs.
evidence: t8.js and t10.js bins text: 'INSTRUMENTS | 1 / 1 slots', 'PROPULSION | 3 / 0 slots'.
cause: js/ui-design.js:2072. When used > 0, `slot` is non-null, so the noRoom && n branch is dead. Plural is hard-coded.
fix_hint: Check max === 0 before the slot text and pluralise on max.

verdict.note: Ran v11.js. IGY, Explorer body plus one part of each kind: bins read 'INSTRUMENTS 1 / 1 slots', 'RADIO 1 / 1 slots', 'ATTITUDE 1 / 1 slots' (wrong plural). New Space, Explorer body (no propulsion slots) plus prop-green-small reads 'PROPULSION 1 / 0 slots'; with three propulsion parts it reads 'PROPULSION 3 / 0 slots'. The 'N on board, no room' wording never shows. Root cause: js/ui-design.js:2068-2072. bodySummary always returns a slot object, and once used > 0, `slot` stays non-null, so noRoom is false and the `noRoom ? (n ? n + ' on board, no room' ...)` branch is dead for n > 0. 'slots' is hard-coded plural. The over-full bin is still marked red (.need), so the meaning comes through; this is wording only.

title: Readiness assembly animation plays off-screen and finishes before a phone or 200% zoom player can scroll to it
repro: iPhone 13 profile (390x664) or 640x400. Reach the Launch Pad with a complete design.
expected: The staggered assembly of the satellite is visible when the screen opens, as on desktop.

title: Event choices hide the cost of the safe option, and the orange highlight lands on the risky option in some events
repro: Fly the working 1958 design (LEO, Juno) at default speed until an event appears (kid9.js: Solar storm). Fly it again with the first (orange) choice for every event (kid13.js: Software bug).
expected: Each choice shows its trade (what you lose, what you risk), so the decision has stakes and the outcome feels earned.
actual: Solar storm: 'Shut instruments down' (orange, focused, no cost shown) against 'Keep observing / 40% chance of losing the computer'. The safe option secretly costs a month (data/events.js:48 lose_months: 1), so it looks free and the choice is obvious. After the choice the log only repeats the label ('Solar storm: Shut instruments down'), with no consequence. Software bug: the orange first button is the risky 'Upload the fix now' (20% chance of losing the computer); in kid13 it failed the clock and ended the mission at month 34 of 36. Because the orange style is applied by position, it reads as a recommendation that sometimes points at danger. A solar storm during a radiation-belt mission is also a science opportunity, but no upside is ever offered.
evidence: (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/12-event-1.png; kid9.js log 'after choice log top: Solar storm: Shut instruments down'; kid13.js 'Software bug: Upload the fix now (Clock and command receiver failed)'
cause: js/ui-mission.js:135-140 builds a sub-line only for fail_chance and sets primary: i === 0; answer() (from line 160) logs only the label. data/events.js lists the risky option first for software-bug (line 85) and the safe one first for solar-storm (line 48).
fix_hint: Give every choice a cost line built from its effect ('lose 1 month, about -4 pts', '-$0.3M', 'science x0.6'). Drop the primary style on event choices. After the choice, log what it cost ('Instruments off for a month: -4 pts').

title: The budget never matters in 1958: the most a flyable design can cost is about 5% of the $90M bar
screen: 3 Build / 4 Launch vehicle budget bar, Debrief 'Value for money', Campaign treasury
repro: IGY Initial Feasibility. Compute the cost of every flyable 1958 design (probe1.js, probe4.js). Pick Juno or Vanguard on the Rocket Yard. Fly two campaign flights (judge10.js).
expected: Budget is one of the 'four bars' the SPEC says every part pulls on, so it should constrain some choice.
actual: The 3-star designs cost $3.6M to $4.14M of $90M (Geiger, tape recorder, Juno: $4.14M). Even an overweight, unflyable 'everything' design costs only $4.29M. The budget bar stays near 5%, so a part's price never affects a choice. On the Rocket Yard, Vanguard saves $0.5M (worthless against $90M) but leaves a 4% mass margin (Margins 7.5/15, against 15/15 with Juno), so the trade is one-sided. After a win, TRY THIS says 'reach it on a smaller budget'. Campaign: the treasury went $90M -> $90.1M after a net -$2.1M flight, then to $101.8M after the second. The Trade Space ($20M) and Point Design ($18M) IGY tiers were locked on a fresh save and not played; from the data, the $4.3M ceiling is under their budgets too.
evidence: probe4.js costs (geiger+clock 3.96, scint+clock 4.06, geiger+tape 4.14); probe1.js tot3 cost_musd 4.29; kid13.js (Vanguard: MARGINS 7.5/15) against kid9.js (Juno: 15/15); judge10.js 'Treasury now $90.1M', '$101.8M'; data/tiers.js comment says the $90M is sized for 'the $69.75M rocket to geostationary orbit'
cause: data/tiers.js: one budget per tier for every era (training 90, standard 20, expert 18), sized for 2026 launch prices; 1958 parts and rockets cost $0.02M to $3M.
fix_hint: Scale budgets by era (for example a 1958 Initial Feasibility of about $5M, so Juno against Vanguard and the tape recorder become real trades), or scale prices by era. Drop the 'smaller budget' TRY THIS when spending is under 20%.

title: REDESIGN lands on Build with stale guidance and does not point at the fix the debrief just named
repro: Fly the battery-only 1958 design. The debrief says 'TRY THIS: ... Fit the early silicon solar cells so the Sun keeps it running.' Press REDESIGN (kid9.js).
expected: Build opens with the named part's bin selected or highlighted, and the guidance repeats the suggested change.
actual: Build opens with the objective 'OBJECTIVE: Go to the Launch Pad for the readiness review.' and the team line 'The instrument makes more data than the radio can send home.' The POWER bin is neither selected nor highlighted, and the TRY THIS text is not shown on Build, so a player who skimmed the debrief is told the design is ready and pointed at the radio.
evidence: kid9.js: 'BUILD on redesign TEAM: ... The instrument makes more data than the radio can send home.' and 'OBJECTIVE: OBJECTIVE: Go to the Launch Pad for the readiness review.'; (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/11-redesign.png
cause: The waypoint (js/ui-design.js:2247-2257) only checks runChecks blockers, and battery-only is a warning; storyBuild picks its line from the current checks, not from the debrief's limiting factor.
fix_hint: Carry the debrief's limiting factor and suggested part into Build: preselect that bin, outline the suggested card, and set the objective to 'Try this: fit Early silicon solar cells'.

title: Mixed messages: a target-beating flight that unlocked a new era is called a failure, and a 4%-of-target flight gets full Events and New Science points
screen: 7 Debrief (score card, team line, notebook), 6 Mission log
repro: (a) Fly the working 1958 design with the first choice for every event until the software bug fails the computer (kid13.js). (b) Fly the battery-only design (kid8.js).
expected: The verdict reads the same everywhere: stars, team line, notebook and log agree.
actual: (a) '128 of 100 points', two stars, 'TRADE SPACE UNLOCKED', 'NEW ERA: NIMBUS (1964)', and at the same time the team says 'We lost it in flight. Find out why before we fly again.' and the notebook says 'The satellite failed.' A 13-year-old cannot tell whether they won. (b) '4 of 100 points', 0 stars, yet 'EVENTS 10 / 10' (no event happened) and 'NEW SCIENCE 10 / 10' bring the score to 31, and the mission log said 'Signal ends. Mission complete.' Also, the empty-star stamp is red outline stars on cream, which at a glance reads as three red stars.
evidence: kid13.js debrief dump; kid8.js debrief dump and mission log; (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/10-debrief.png, (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/16-debrief-open.png
cause: The debrief and notebook story lines (storyDebrief, storyNotebook, js/ui-design.js:604-660) key on ended_early or failure, not on the target being met; the scoring gives full Events credit when no event happens.
fix_hint: When the target is met, use 'Goal met before we lost it in month 34' and a success notebook line. Score Events as 'n/a' (or scale it by science share) when no event happened. Log 'Signal lost' instead of 'Mission complete' on an early end.

title: Campaign money text contradicts itself: 'pays about $9.7M', then $0.87M, then '$1M... the payout was large', and a silent grant
screen: Campaign hub, 1 Briefing, 4 Launch vehicle, 7 Debrief
repro: Fresh save at 390px. Press [data-key="campaign-training"], read the hub, then START A MISSION and fly the battery-only radiation design on Vanguard. Fly a second time after buying Silicon solar cells (judge3.js, judge8.js, judge10.js).
expected: The expected payout matches across the hub, the Build screen and the debrief, and every treasury change is explained.
actual: The hub says 'Next mission pays about $9.7M' and the briefing card 'Pays $9.7M'. The Rocket Yard says 'Expected payout $0.87M, cost $3M, net -$2.1M'. The debrief says 'PAYOUT $1M ... This was a first real look at the topic... That is why the payout was large.', then 'Treasury now $90.1M' (up, after a -$2.1M flight, because an unmentioned $2M grant arrived). The second flight says 'This was a first real look at the topic' again, although knowledge went 5% -> 64%. The offer sentence starts in lower case ('the National Academy of Sciences wants...'), and the campaign debrief header reads 'INITIAL FEASIBILITY · SCORE 35', not CAMPAIGN.
evidence: judge3.js hub dump; judge5.js launcher text ('Expected payout $0.87M, cost $3M, net -$2.1M'); judge8.js and judge10.js debrief dumps; (scratch)/sweep/engage/judge/26-camp-debrief-full.png
cause: data/campaign.js grant_musd 2 is applied in js/mission.js:869-872 but not shown in the debrief text; the hub figure is the payout at full target; the 'first real look' sentence is not tied to the knowledge share; the offer text is built from the client name in lower case.
fix_hint: Show the grant as its own line ('Agency grant +$2M'). Have the hub say 'up to $9.7M for a full-target flight'. Pick the payout sentence from the actual knowledge gain. Capitalise the start of the offer sentence.

title: Campaign Launch Vehicle screen is 531px wide on a 390px phone (locked-rocket tags do not wrap)

expected: No sideways scrolling at 390px; every other campaign screen measured 390.

With mobile emulation the layout viewport grows to innerWidth 531, and Playwright's tap on GO TO LAUNCH PAD was repeatedly reported as intercepted; a plain click at 390px non-mobile worked. evidence: judge6.js: { iw: 531, vv: 390, docW: 531, wide: [ 'SPAN.tag bad right=402 ...', 'right=510 ...', 'right=531 ...' ] }; judge8.js WIDTH lines (390 for the other screens); (scratch)/sweep/engage/judge/25-camp-launcher-wide.png

title: FIRST 2 MINUTES: the map repeats the same instruction four times (150 words), and Build opens on the wrong bin for its first line
repro: Fresh save, start IGY Initial Feasibility, skip the intro and read the map. Continue to Build and read the team line and the selected bin (kid1.js, kid4.js).
expected: One clear instruction per screen, and coaching that matches what is on screen.
actual: The map has 150 words. 'Go to Mission Control and pick a job' appears in the header objective, the prompt box ('Follow the gold route. Go to Mission Control and pick a job.'), the sidebar OBJECTIVE and the place list ('Pick a job for the satellite'), on top of the team line ('Begin at Mission Control. The gold route leads the way.'), the hint ('Walk with the arrow keys or WASD...') and a KEYS box. The map is a stop between every step and asks no decision on the first run. On Build, the team says 'Every satellite needs a body to hold its parts.' while the INSTRUMENTS bin is preselected.
evidence: kid1.js MAP dump (150 words); kid4.js BUILD dump; (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/02-map.png, (scratch)/sweep/engage/kid/05-build.png
cause: drawMap (js/ui-design.js:2382+) renders the objective, the prompt, the side objective and the place list from the same doText(); drawBuild starts on the instrument bin while storyBuild's first line asks for a body.
fix_hint: Keep one instruction (the prompt box with its button) and drop the duplicate sidebar OBJECTIVE. On the first run, consider going straight from the intro to Mission Control. Preselect the STRUCTURE bin while the body line is showing.
